newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's BBC bank plans to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's BBC bank plans to raise capital.

text.p: Banque Beyrouth pour le Commerce (BBC) plans to raise its capital by 35 to 40 billion Lebanese pounds ($25.9 million) from 15 billion, Chairman and General Manager Rifaat el-Nimer told Reuters on Friday.
"We want to raise our capital 35 to 40 billion pounds from 15 billion at present," Nimer said.
"All the shareholders are in agreement on the capital increase, but the question is by how much, 35 or 40 billion," he added.

Nimer said the increase would come from shareholders' cash contributions and could take at least two months to be decided, adding that the plan still needed central bank approval and a shareholders' assembly tp discuss the plan.
Nimer and his son Rami and a third Lebanese investor hold a majority stake in BBC. The rest is owned by 12 Lebanese and Arab investors.
BBC said it ranked 15th among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks in terms of customer deposits in 1996.
